description: Demetrius I Poliorcetes, “the Besieger,” became famous for deploying enormous siege towers designed to overwhelm the defenses of fortified cities. His most celebrated machine was the Helepolis, used during the siege of Rhodes in 305–304 BC: a multi-storied, iron-plated wooden tower mounted on wheels and packed with catapults, bolt-shooters, and troops firing from protected galleries. These colossal engines combined intimidation with concentrated missile fire, allowing attackers to dominate walls and support assaults at close range, and they became symbols of the extraordinary scale and engineering ambition of Hellenistic siege warfare.
